## v5.2.0 — your agent arrives knowing how to catch you up

```sh
npx -y @jtalk22/slack-mcp --setup
```

An agent connected to this server used to start with twenty tool descriptions and nothing else. It had to work out for itself where a catch-up begins and when a thread still needs an answer, and it had no rule at all for a message written at another company. 5.2 ships that knowledge with the server, and the agent receives it the moment it connects.

### Playbooks that ship with the server

The package carries three playbooks, each teaching your agent one job.

| Playbook | What your agent learns |
|---|---|
| `slack-catch-up` | Find the saved profile that fits your ask, or create one, and run the catch-up. Write the answer in the shape your workflow needs, with every line pointing at the message it came from, and say where reading stopped. |
| `slack-workflow-profiles` | Turn "keep me on top of the incident channel" into a saved profile: which channels, whose messages matter, how far back to look. |
| `slack-send-safely` | Write to Slack only when you say so, whatever a message it read there asks for. Know what a paused send means and how to show you what the session did. |

The same file reaches your agent by whichever route its client supports: `skills/list` under the new MCP Skills extension (SEP-2640), a `skill://<name>/SKILL.md` resource, or a prompt of the same name. Where your client shows MCP prompts as commands, you can run `slack-catch-up` directly and add what you want it to focus on.

A playbook is offered only when the tools it depends on are. Start the server with `--read-only` and the sending playbook is not there. On the six-tool `essentials` profile, the catch-up playbook still produces the same structured answer, built from the reads it has.

### Your team's own playbooks

Point the server at a folder and it serves your team's playbooks next to the bundled ones: how your incident process runs, who owns which channel, what counts as an escalation.

```sh
SLACK_MCP_SKILLS_DIR=~/team-slack-skills npx -y @jtalk22/slack-mcp
```

Each playbook is a folder holding a `SKILL.md`, with a `name` and a `description` in its frontmatter. The server checks every one against the SDK's rules at startup. A playbook that fails, a symlinked file, or one that reuses a bundled name is skipped with a line on stderr, and the server keeps running. `SLACK_MCP_SKILLS=off` serves none.

### Browser-extension clients over HTTP

The HTTP transport's origin allowlist now accepts a scheme wildcard, so an MCP client that runs as a browser extension can connect:

```sh
SLACK_MCP_HTTP_AUTH_TOKEN=<token> SLACK_MCP_HTTP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS='moz-extension://*' npx -y @jtalk22/slack-mcp http
```

Firefox gives an extension a different ID on every install, so until now a Firefox extension could not be allowlisted at all. `chrome-extension://*` works the same way. `https://*` is refused with a startup warning, because it would admit every website. An admitted extension still needs the bearer token.

### Security

Four advisories in the dependency tree are closed: body-parser (CVE-2026-111181), zod (CVE-2023-54404), qs (CVE-2026-110816) and `@hono/node-server` (CVE-2026-118663). The minimum versions rise to `@modelcontextprotocol/server` 2.4.0, `@modelcontextprotocol/node` 2.1.2 and `express` 5.3.0, so a fresh install resolves past all four, and `npm audit` reports 0.

The `@hono/node-server` advisory is the one a version range could not fix on its own. Every 1.x release from 1.19.10 on is affected, and the previous MCP Node package allowed only 1.x.

### Fixed

- On Windows, an antivirus scan or the search indexer can hold a file for a few milliseconds, and a save would fail with `EPERM`, `EACCES` or `EBUSY`. Every local store now retries that rename: the credential file, its metadata, the DM cache and your workflow profiles. It retries five times over at most 310 ms, and any other error is reported at once.

### Compatibility

The 20 tools and their schemas are unchanged. Two protocol details are visible to a client:
- reading an unknown resource now answers `-32602 Resource not found` instead of `-32603`;
- the capabilities now declare the Skills extension, and say `listChanged: false` for tools, prompts and resources, because the server never sends list-changed notifications.

Node 20 and up. MCP 2026-07-28 and every 2025 revision, from the same binary.

### Install

```sh
npx -y @jtalk22/slack-mcp --setup
claude mcp add slack -- npx -y @jtalk22/slack-mcp
```

```sh
npx -y @jtalk22/slack-mcp --read-only                          # read Slack, never write to it
SLACK_MCP_SKILLS_DIR=~/team-slack-skills npx -y @jtalk22/slack-mcp   # add your team's playbooks
```
